faqs.a: No. It only changes whitespace and line breaks: indentation, newlines after braces and semicolons, and spacing after keywords. Your strings, comments, identifiers and logic are preserved byte for byte. Still, for production code, run your tests after formatting, as with any formatter.
faqs.q: Does formatting change what my code does?

faqs.a: Because the formatter masks them before touching layout. Strings, template literals, regular expressions and comments are extracted first, the code skeleton is formatted, then they are restored untouched. That is why a brace inside a string never breaks the indentation.
faqs.q: Why are my strings and comments never broken?

code-formatter.formula:
JavaScript: tokenize (strings, template literals, regex, comments masked) -> brace depth +1 on {, -1 on } -> newline after ; only when parenthesis depth = 0 -> space after if/for/while/switch/catch keywords.
CSS: one declaration per line, space after : inside rules, nested @media blocks indented, selectors split on top-level commas.
HTML: block elements get newline + indent, inline elements stay on the text line, script/style contents kept raw.
howTo: Pick the language tab: JavaScript, CSS or HTML.
Paste your messy or minified code into the input box, or press Sample to try an example.
Choose 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs. The formatted output updates live below.
Review the output, then copy it or download it as a .js, .css or .html file.
If the output looks wrong on exotic syntax, check the Limitations section; the original is never modified.
keyFacts: A lightweight beautifier for JavaScript, CSS and HTML that fixes layout without touching logic.
String-aware tokenizing: quotes, template literals, regular expressions and comments are masked before formatting and restored untouched.
JavaScript: brace-aware indentation, newlines after semicolons outside for-loop parentheses, and spacing after keywords like if and for.
CSS: one declaration per line, a space after each colon inside rules, nested @media blocks indented, selectors split on top-level commas.
HTML: block elements get their own indented lines while inline elements stay on the text line; script and style contents are kept raw.
Formatting is live: every keystroke re-formats instantly, entirely in your browser.

limitations: Lightweight, not Prettier: it does not normalize quotes, semicolons, operator spacing or trailing commas.
Spacing around operators (+, =, =>) is left as you wrote it.
Code inside template-literal ${} expressions is not re-formatted.
Very exotic or invalid syntax may format oddly; always review the output before shipping.
